speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you've been dealing with a chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis; to distinguish between causes like asthma, COPD, or post-infectious bronchiectasis, we must start with your history. Have you noticed if your cough worsens significantly in the early morning or after exposure to cold air?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis.

The history of a chronic cough with copious, thick, purulent (yellow-green) sputum for 11 years, along with recurrent bronchitis requiring antibiotics, is highly specific for bronchiectasis. Please confirm if you have ever had a CT scan showing "tram-tracking" or "ring shadows," or if you have experienced hemoptysis (coughing up blood) in the past.
